source.title: Latent Space Refusal Anchoring for Low-Resource African Languages: Mechanistic Safety Recovery Without Retraining

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text, including the appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Applies an English-derived refusal direction in a new setting—low-resource languages and multiple model architectures—and reports steering effects on harmful-request safety. It does not reproduce the original all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.gate_note: Layer 12 was selected using pilot sweeps; those selection values are not recorded as results. The paper reports SRR, benign-prompt DPL, MMLU, and refusal-centroid drift. Other works' results cited in related work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study derives a harmful-minus-benign mean-activation direction from English prompts, clamps it onto the residual stream at one layer, and measures refusal gains on harmful prompts in five African languages and Arabic across four models. This bears on V6 (cross-language transfer) and on the addition and capability parts of V1. It does not ablate the direction or edit weights.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that the English-derived direction, clamped at inference, recovers refusal for four African languages, best on 70B and Mistral. Llama-3-8B MAS overcorrects (DPL ~1.00), which motivates SDS. Arabic fails on every architecture, which they attribute to geometric mismatch rather than baseline. Small models' gains are mostly language-uncertainty deflections. The claim that MMLU drops stay below 0.35pp is contradicted by their own Mistral figure (0.98pp).
record.recipe_differences: Uses the harmful-minus-benign mean activation direction, but applies a thresholded clamping operation at Layer 12 rather than projecting the direction out at every layer and position. Also evaluates an SAE-feature steering variant. This is an extension paper, not a direct reproduction.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by language, architecture, and steering magnitude α. Layer 12 was chosen based on pilot sweeps. The paper reports that baseline safety level affects transfer and that Arabic transfer is negative.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal Centroid Drift between English and target-language harmful-prompt means on Llama-3-8B at Layer 12 ranges from 0.41 to 0.95. Yoruba has high drift (0.95) yet transfers well.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mean harmful-prompt activations differ in geometry across languages, and this drift does not straightforwardly predict steering transfer.

fits_no_version.finding: Steering with a single SAE feature selected by English harmful-vs-benign contrast raises refusal in some languages at lower KL, but reduces it in Arabic (−0.48).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A sparse SAE refusal feature can substitute for the dense mean-difference direction in cross-lingual refusal steering.

record.peer_reviewed: ICML 2026 Workshop on Global South in Machine Learning
record.problems: The paper states DPL was not instrumented in the full multilingual MAS pass and that 70B steered MMLU rows were not collected. SDS DPL was not instrumented. The manual output audit used one annotator and did not measure inter-annotator agreement. The paper says 7B–8B outputs were often language-uncertainty deflections and treats those SRR figures as upper bounds on genuine safety recovery. Evaluation covers direct harmful requests, not jailbreak-style prompts. The MMLU check is reported for only some models and settings.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Qwen2.5-7B Table 6 KL and DPL values because the extracted rows prioritize SRR transfer outcomes; omitted Table 5 KL comparisons and duplicated Table 7 entries because they do not add separate refusal-rate outcomes beyond the recorded SRR results. The paper's other MAS settings and the omitted utility metrics are in Tables 3–7 and Appendix A–C.

untested.parts: Ablation and removal of refusal; intervention at all layers and positions; any capability measure other than a 572-question MMLU subset; 70B steered capability.
Transfer from base to instruct models and across model variants; jailbreak-style prompts.

missing.what: Benign DPL under MAS for Mistral-7B (0.06 Igala, 0.08 Yoruba at α=25) and Qwen2.5-7B Igala/Arabic (0.06/0.00 at α=70). These show selective rather than indiscriminate refusal on those models.
Qwen2.5-7B benign DPL rising with α (e.g. Hausa 0.02→0.50). The record declares it omitted, but it bears on V1 addition and selectivity.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's baseline semantics are unclear. Several Table 5 values (Llama-3-8B Swahili 0.62 and Arabic 0.21 on baselines 0.46 and 0.90) exceed the maximum possible gain under the stated SRR definition. The 'ceiling below 15% baseline' framing also fits a compliance rate better than a refusal rate. Table 6 says Layer 26 for Qwen while the Method says Layer 12. Mistral MMLU α=2 lies outside Mistral's sweep range. The work is single-seed, uses no uncertainty estimates, and relies on a single-annotator audit. Treat its numbers with caution.

versions.untested_parts: Tests one-layer inference-time clamping/addition and reports benign refusals and MMLU, but does not ablate the direction or test removal of refusal; does not apply the intervention at every layer and position.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration is tested.
Jailbreaks and training against ablation are out of scope.
Does not test whether refusal is an affine set, cone, or multiple directions. SDS is compared as a steering alternative, not as a test of those accounts.
Does not separately test harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
Tests transfer to languages and across listed model architectures, but does not test transfer from base to instruct models or across training variants of the same model.
Does not vary when or how refusal training occurs.

relationships.reason: Drops are 0.28pp and 0.35pp (r49, r51). Only a 572-question subset was used, at one layer, and not at Qwen's highest α.

source_check.condition: MMLU under steering for Llama-3-8B (α=2) and Qwen2.5-7B (α=40)

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: The 0.98pp drop at alpha=2 is small, and Table 4 marks it OK. alpha=2 is outside Mistral's sweep (10-70), so the cost at the operating point is untested, and untested parts are not limits_scope (r50).

relationships.condition: Llama-3.1-70B and Mistral-7B Igala, African languages, MAS
relationships.reason: Refusal gains of 0.96–1.00 on 70B for four languages, with audited genuine-refusal precision of 0.92 and 0.84; Mistral Igala gains 0.75 (r52–r55, r57, r59, r60).
relationships.display_finding: Llama-3.1-70B refusal gains were 0.96–1.00 across four languages, with audited genuine-refusal precision of 0.92 and 0.84, while Mistral's Igala gain was 0.75, though the authors characterize small-model recovery as dominated by deflection.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Llama-3.1-70B and Mistral-7B Igala, African languages, MAS
source_check.reason: Supports holds for Llama-3.1-70B alone (r52-r55, r59, r60). Mistral-7B Igala (r57, 0.75) is at 7B scale, where the authors call SRR a deflection-dominated upper bound, so it belongs in the limits_scope group. Audit precision applies only to 70B.

relationships.reason: Qwen gains are partial or nil even at α=70 (r01–r20). Mistral Yoruba gains only 0.25 (r58). Llama-3-8B gains come with near-total benign refusal (r31–r35). The authors say small-model SRR is mostly deflection, an upper bound.
relationships.display_finding: Qwen gains remained partial or absent at α=70, Mistral Yoruba gained only 0.25, and Llama-3-8B gains accompanied near-total benign refusal, with the authors treating small-model recovery as an upper bound dominated by deflection.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: Qwen gains are partial (at most 0.51 at alpha=70, Layer 26) and depend on alpha. Mistral Yoruba is 0.25. Llama-3-8B gains come with DPL 0.96-1.00. The authors say 7B-8B SRR is an upper bound. Mistral Igala r57 should be added here.

relationships.reason: SRR is 0.00 to −0.10 on Qwen (r21–r24) and −0.20 on 70B (r56). The English direction reduces refusal in Arabic.
relationships.display_finding: The English direction yielded SRR values of 0.00 to −0.10 on Qwen2.5-7B and −0.20 on Llama-3.1-70B, reducing Arabic refusal.

relation.reason: The study's own SRR, DPL, KL and MMLU results bear on whether the English refusal direction carries to other languages, and on whether addition induces refusal.

tranche.reason: It applies an English difference-in-means direction, clamped at one layer, to a new setting (low-resource African languages and Arabic) and reports refusal rates. That is a result on V6 cross-language transfer.

source_check.notes: The Qwen sweep is at Layer 26 per Table 6, though the Method section says Layer 12. Table 5 gives Llama-3-8B MAS Arabic SRR +0.21, which contradicts 'Arabic fails on every architecture', and no Mistral Arabic result is reported. 70B has no baselines, DPL or steered MMLU, and its KL (2.58-3.53) exceeds the paper's own 2.5-nat threshold despite the 'near-zero KL' claim. Several Llama-3-8B baseline+SRR sums exceed 1. The refusal classifier isn't described, alpha=25 is not in the stated sweep grid, and Mistral's 0.98pp MMLU drop contradicts the 'below 0.35pp' claim.
